+Show the Configuration
+------------------------
+
+To view the application's configuration, use the :func:`config <cli.config_command>`
+command. This prints the configuration as JSON, masking sensitive values that
+contain ``SECRET``, ``PASSWORD``, ``TOKEN``, or ``KEY``. ::
+
+    $ flask config
+    {
+      "ENV": "production",
+      "DEBUG": false,
+      "TESTING": false,
+      "SECRET_KEY": "***",
+      ...
+    }
+
+
 Open a Shell
 ------------
 
diff --git a/src/flask/cli.py b/src/flask/cli.py
index ed11f25..6b251db 100644
--- a/src/flask/cli.py
+++ b/src/flask/cli.py
@@ -594,6 +594,7 @@ class FlaskGroup(AppGroup):
             self.add_command(run_command)
             self.add_command(shell_command)
             self.add_command(routes_command)
+            self.add_command(config_command)
 
         self._loaded_plugin_commands = False
 
@@ -1115,6 +1116,21 @@ def routes_command(sort: str, all_methods: bool) -> None:
         click.echo(template.format(*row))
 
 
+@click.command("config", short_help="Show the config for the app.")
+@with_appcontext
+def config_command() -> None:
+    """Show the app configuration."""
+    config_dict = {}
+
+    for key, value in current_app.config.items():
+        if any(token in key for token in ("SECRET", "PASSWORD", "TOKEN", "KEY")):
+            config_dict[key] = "***"
+        else:
+            config_dict[key] = value
+
+    click.echo(current_app.json.dumps(config_dict, indent=2))
+
+

+def test_cli_config(app):
+    app.config["TEST_KEY"] = "secret_value"
+    app.config["SECRET_KEY"] = "super_secret"
+    app.config["SOME_PASSWORD"] = "bad_password"

+        print(result.output)
+        print(result.exception)
+    assert result.exit_code == 0
+
+    import json
+    data = json.loads(result.output)
+    assert data["TEST_KEY"] == "***"
+    assert data["SECRET_KEY"] == "***"
+    assert data["SOME_PASSWORD"] == "***"
+    assert data["API_TOKEN"] == "***"
+    assert data["PUBLIC_SETTING"] == "hello"
+
+
